For each 1930 World Cup squad player, I identified the top-flight leagues they played in throughout their entire career and checked whether any of those leagues had a formally recognised season-long best player award that the player won.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean a national or regional top-flight professional or semi-professional football competition within a single country (excluding cup competitions, continental competitions, and international tournaments). For each player in every 1934 World Cup squad, the domestic leagues in which they played club football throughout their entire career were identified, then each such league was checked for the existence of a formally recognized season-long best-player award (whether given by the league, players' union, or press). Every major relevant award in the participating nations (Italian Gran Galà/AIC, German kicker Footballer of the Year, French UNFP award, Swedish Guldbollen, Belgian Golden Shoe, Hungarian Footballer of the Year, Austrian Footballer of the Year, etc.) was established only after essentially all 1934 World Cup players had retired from professional football, and no pre-1934 season-long domestic league best player award in any of the sixteen participating nations could be confirmed; therefore no qualifying player was found.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any national or regional first-division professional or semi-professional football league (including historical competitions such as the pre-unification German Oberligen, pre-1960s state championships in Brazil, the Argentine Primera División, etc.) in any country where the player held a club contract. Best-player award was restricted to a season-long award voted by journalists, players or the league body, as opposed to top-scorer, goalkeeper, young-player or cup-specific honours. For each squad player I traced the full club career and the award history of every league in which they played, checking whether a qualifying award existed during the player's active years and whether documented evidence of a win exists.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any top-division professional or amateur national or regional league competition in which the player regularly competed as a club footballer, in any country. For each squad player I considered the full arc of their club careers — which countries and top divisions they played in, and what season-long best-player awards those leagues operated (whether given by the league, the press, or a players' association) — then checked whether the player had won such an award in any season, regardless of timing relative to the 1950 World Cup.

"Domestic league" means the top professional or semi-professional national league competition of the country in which a player competed at club level (e.g., Nemzeti Bajnokság in Hungary, La Liga in Spain). I considered every country's league in which a squad player held a registered playing career, then checked whether that league had a season-long best-player award voted by press, players, or the league body, and whether the player won it in any season of his career.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any top-tier national football league competition in which a player participated as a club footballer, in any country and at any point in his career. For each squad member identified from the 1958 FIFA World Cup rosters, I considered every country's top division in which he played club football and checked whether that league had (or has) a season-long best player award — regardless of the awarding body (league, players' union, or press) — and whether the player won it.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any national professional or semi-professional football league competition (and its successor competitions under renamed or restructured forms) in any country in which the player was registered as a club player, including top divisions of national leagues such as the English First Division, Soviet Top League, Bundesliga, Serie A, Nemzeti Bajnokság, Czechoslovak First League, and Campeonato Brasileiro. For each squad member I considered every country in which they played club football at any point in their career, identified any season-long best player award associated with that league (whether awarded by the governing body, the players' association, or the sports press), and checked whether the player had won it in any season before, during, or after the 1962 World Cup.

"Domestic league" means the top-tier professional football league of the country in which a player was registered as a club footballer in a given season, excluding continental competitions (UEFA Champions League, etc.), domestic cups, and international/FIFA/UEFA-level awards. For each squad player I considered every country's first division in which he played club matches at any point in his career, then checked whether that league operated a season-long best-player award voted by the press, players' union, or the league body itself, and whether the player won it.

"Domestic league" means a top-division national football league competition in any country (e.g. Bundesliga, First Division/Football League, Eredivisie, La Liga, Serie A, Campeonato Brasileiro). For each squad player I identified which top-flight league(s) they played in across their entire career, then checked whether that league has (or had) a season-long best-player award voted by journalists, players, or the league itself, and whether the player won it in any season before, during, or after 1970.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any top-tier professional or semi-professional national league competition in which a player regularly competed as a club footballer, in any country and at any point in his career. For each squad member, I considered every club for which he played (from career records) and determined the top division of that country, then checked whether that league operated a season-long best-player award (by the league body, players' association, or the specialist football press of that country), and whether the player had won it in any season before, during, or after the 1974 World Cup.

"Domestic league" means a national top-division professional (or top-tier) football league in any country, including leagues that were later renamed or reorganised (e.g., the Campeonato Brasileiro, which was known by several names). For each squad player I identified every country in which he played club football at any point in his career, looked up whether that league has a season-long best-player award voted by journalists, players, or the league body, and checked whether he won it; continental and international awards (e.g., Ballon d'Or) and subcategory awards (top scorer, goalkeeper, young player) were excluded.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any top-tier (or primary) national football league competition in which the player appeared as a club professional, in any country, at any point in his career. For each squad player I identified every country's league he played in professionally, then determined whether that league had a season-long best-player award (regardless of the awarding body — the league itself, a players' union, or the press), and checked whether he won it in any season.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any national top-division professional football league competition in which a player participated during his club career; association/federation-level national player-of-the-year awards tied to that top-flight competition (such as the Bola de Ouro, Piłkarz Roku, Fußballer des Jahres, Trophée UNFP, PFA Players' Player of the Year, Profvoetballer van het Jaar, Don Balón Award, Premio AIC and Årets Fodboldspiller) were counted where they honour the best performer in that domestic league season, and each player's full career was traced across all countries in which he played club football to identify every relevant league and its best-player award.

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any national top-flight club football league competition in which a player participated during his professional career (before, during, or after the 1990 World Cup), including leagues that have since been renamed or dissolved (e.g., the Soviet Top League, Yugoslav First Federal League, Football League First Division). For each of the 494+ squad players across the 24 qualifying nations in 1990, I identified every country and league tier at the top level in which they played club football, then assessed whether that league's principal season-long best player award existed and was won by that player in any season.

"Domestic league" means a national top-division professional football league in any country, excluding continental competitions (UEFA Champions League, Copa Libertadores, etc.) and international tournaments. For each squad player I considered all club career stints across all countries and checked whether the highest-division league in each of those countries had a season-long best player award, and whether the player won it at any point during their career.

"Domestic league" means a national top-division professional football league in any country (e.g., Serie A in Italy, La Liga in Spain, Ligue 1 in France, the Premier League in England, the Eredivisie in the Netherlands, the Campeonato Brasileiro in Brazil, etc.). For each squad player I considered every top-flight league they played in during their entire career and identified the season-long best player award(s) associated with that league — whether given by the league body, the players' union, or the press — and checked whether the player won it in any season before, during, or after the 1998 World Cup.

"Domestic league" means the top-tier professional football league in any country in which a player competed as a club footballer at any point in his career. For each squad player I identified every club he played for, determined the top division of that country, researched what season-long best-player award that league presents (or presented), and checked whether he won it in any season of his career. Awards such as Don Balón (La Liga), Oscar del Calcio/AIC Award (Serie A), PFA Players' Player of the Year and FWA Footballer of the Year (English top division), Trophée UNFP (Ligue 1), and SFWA Player of the Year (Scottish Premier League) were treated as qualifying awards; purely international, continental, monthly, positional, top-scorer, and young-player awards were excluded.

"Domestic league" means the top-tier professional football league of any country in which a player played club football, excluding continental or international competitions. For each player in the 2006 World Cup squads I identified all clubs he played for across his career, determined each club's top-tier national league, identified the season-long best-player award(s) of those leagues (by any name, as given by the league, players' union, or press), and confirmed—based on historical records—whether he won it in any season before, during, or after 2006.

"Domestic league" means a fully professional or semi-professional national football division (any tier) in any country in which the player appeared as a registered club player; continental competitions (UEFA Champions League, Copa Libertadores, etc.) and international team awards are excluded. For each player, every club career stint was traced to identify which national leagues applied, and then the recognised season-long best-player award(s) of those leagues—whether named after a trophy, a magazine, a players' union vote, or a league-body vote—were checked against the player's career history.

"Domestic league" means a national professional first-division football league in which the player played club football at any stage of their career (before, during, or after the 2014 World Cup). For each player, the relevant leagues were determined by tracking their club career across all countries in which they played — identifying each country's top professional football competition and the season-long individual award given by that league, its governing body, its players' union, or the leading domestic sports publication for best player of the season (excluding position-specific, monthly, young player, top scorer, and cup/continental awards).

"Domestic league" was taken to mean any top-division professional football league in a sovereign country (e.g. Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Brasileirão, Ekstraklasa, K League 1, etc.), as distinct from cup competitions, international club competitions, or continental awards. For each squad player I considered every professional club league tier he played in at any point in his career and checked whether that league's season-long best player award (by whatever name — PFA Players' Player of the Year, FWA Footballer of the Year, LFP/LaLiga Best Player, Kicker Footballer of the Year, UNFP Player of the Year, Bola de Ouro, etc.) was ever won by him.

'Domestic league' was taken to mean any national top-flight professional football league in which a player competed as a club player (e.g. Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1, Primeira Liga, Brasileirão), and the relevant leagues for each player were determined by tracing each squad member's full club career history; for each such league the recognised season-long best-player honour (whether given by the league body, the players' union, the press, or a sponsor — but not monthly/weekly, young-player, goalkeeper, top-scorer, cup, or continental awards) was then checked against the player's record.

"Domestic league" means a top-flight national football league competition within a single country (e.g., Premier League in England, La Liga in Spain, Bundesliga in Germany, Ligue 1 in France, Serie A in Italy, Brasileirão in Brazil, MLS in the USA), excluding continental club competitions (UEFA Champions League, etc.) and international tournaments. For each player I traced all club career stints across all countries, identified the top-flight league in each country, and checked whether that league's season-long best player award (by whatever name — PFA Players' Player, FWA Footballer of the Year, UNFP Player of the Year, Kicker award, Don Balón/Marca award, Trofeo Alfredo di Stéfano, Bola de Ouro, AIC award, MLS MVP, etc.) was ever won by that player in any season.
